blocks.text: Public discourse surrounding Pax Silica has frequently focused on technology, critical minerals, semiconductor production and participation in emerging global supply chains. However, a closer examination of the issues raised reveals a fundamentally different debate. At its core, Pax Silica is not merely a technological project but a political, economic, environmental and ethical question concerning land, water, energy, sovereignty, Indigenous rights and democratic consent. The controversy centers on whether the Philippine state should transform ancestral and agricultural lands into mineral-processing zones primarily serving external geopolitical and industrial interests.
